target_isolation: Separate empty target directory for every build; independent private cache stores per compiler wrapper

trials.cache: warm, different checkout path and changed CLI source

source_change_control.edit: Append KACHE_9112_EDIT_FIRED to CLI about text

job_runtime_isolation_probe.fixture: A library returning 9112 and a binary printing that value, built twice in the same checkout with separate empty targets and private runtime/config directories against one shared object store.
job_runtime_isolation_probe.claim: Private telemetry does not prevent shared compiler-object hits, and the second job does not inherit the first job's cold misses.
job_runtime_isolation_probe.limitation: This two-unit probe proves cache and session behavior, not Harn build latency or complete multi-command job attribution.

limitations: Sequential trials on a shared runner under unrelated CI load; wall times are observations, not a controlled distribution or merge-queue p90.
The first two Kache reports inferred the common target parent as session root; their per-checkout counters were unmeasured. Explicit KACHE_EVENT_ROOT fixed attribution for the source-change control.

The original trials shared runtime state, so a checkout session could span consecutive jobs. The follow-up isolates job runtime state; a long job can still span multiple sessions after five idle minutes, so the finalizer does not claim complete per-job attribution.
This trial builds the CLI; it does not establish workspace test-unit or package-verification latency.
